senses.definition: to help someone learn a subject or skill by explaining and practising it with them
senses.example: She teaches English to young children.

senses.zh: 油；食用油；石油；油画颜料
senses.definition: a thick liquid used in cooking or engines, a fuel from underground, or paint made with oil
senses.example: Heat a little oil in the pan.

senses.definition: to put oil on something so it moves smoothly or is protected
senses.example: Oil the bicycle chain before you ride.

senses.definition: one of two equal parts of something, or one period of a sports match
senses.example: I ate half of the apple.

senses.definition: an amount equal to one of two parts of something
senses.example: Half the students came by bus.

senses.definition: to the extent of one half or partly
senses.example: The bottle is half full.

senses.definition: the set of things happening at a particular time, especially those affecting someone
senses.example: We need to understand the situation before we decide.

senses.definition: not difficult to do or understand, or free from worry and effort
senses.example: This question is easy to answer.

senses.definition: the money needed to buy or do something, or the harm caused by an action
senses.example: The cost of living is rising.

senses.definition: to have a price, or cause someone to lose something valuable
senses.example: The repairs will cost a lot of money.

senses.definition: businesses that make or provide similar goods or services, or sustained hard work
senses.example: She works in the film industry.
senses.note: “勤奋”是较旧或较正式的用法；现代学习先掌握“行业、产业”。

senses.definition: a number, a person of a certain kind, the shape of a body, or a picture in a text
senses.example: Sales figures rose last year.

senses.definition: to think or believe something, calculate an amount, or understand a problem
senses.example: I figured she would arrive by noon.

senses.definition: a public road in a town or city with buildings along it
senses.example: We live on a quiet street.

senses.definition: a picture or likeness, or the idea people have about someone or something
senses.example: The camera captured a clear image.

senses.definition: to produce an image of something, especially with medical or electronic equipment
senses.example: The scanner images the inside of the body.
senses.note: 动词 image 多见于医学或技术语境。

senses.definition: used to refer back to a thing or animal as the one doing or receiving an action, or to emphasize it
senses.example: The door closed by itself.

senses.definition: a device used to speak to someone at a distance
senses.example: I left my phone at home.

senses.definition: to call someone using a phone
senses.example: I'll phone you tonight.

senses.zh: 两者中的任一个；两边各一
senses.definition: one of two choices before a noun, or each of two sides
senses.example: Either answer is acceptable.

senses.definition: one of two people or things, used without a following noun
senses.example: Either of the routes will get us there.

senses.definition: used at the end of a negative statement to add a similar fact
senses.example: I don't know, and she doesn't either.

senses.definition: used with or to connect two choices
senses.example: We can either walk or take the bus.

evidence.note: Cambridge grammar lists determiner, pronoun, adverb, conjunction.

senses.definition: facts or information collected for study, comparison, or use by a computer
senses.example: We collected data from the survey.
senses.note: data 可作复数，也常作不可数集合名词；科研写作需遵循所属领域规范。

senses.zh: 覆盖；遮盖；包含；报道；支付
senses.definition: to put something over another thing, include a topic, report an event, or pay an expense
senses.example: The course covers basic grammar.

senses.definition: something placed over another thing, the outer part of a book, or a new version of a song
senses.example: The book has a bright red cover.

senses.definition: to a noticeable degree, or completely in some uses
senses.example: The film was quite good.
senses.note: 英式 quite good 常表示“还不错”；语气强弱会随口音、上下文和形容词变化。

senses.definition: a drawing or photograph, an image on a screen, or an idea of what something is like
senses.example: She sent me a picture of the dog.

senses.definition: to form an image of something in your mind
senses.example: Picture yourself living by the sea.

senses.zh: 清楚的；明确的；透明的；晴朗的
senses.definition: easy to see or understand, without cloud or confusion, or allowing light through
senses.example: Her explanation was clear.

senses.definition: to remove something, become free of something, or receive official permission
senses.example: Please clear the table after dinner.

senses.definition: with nothing blocking the way; usually in fixed phrases
senses.example: The plane flew clear of the storm.

senses.zh: 练习；实践；做法；诊所业务
senses.definition: repeated activity to improve a skill, the actual use of an idea, a customary way of doing something, or a professional business
senses.example: Regular practice helped her speak more confidently.

senses.definition: to do something repeatedly to improve it, carry it out, or work in a profession
senses.example: She practices speaking English every day.
senses.note: 美式动词拼 practice；英式动词通常拼 practise。

senses.definition: one part of something, a single item, or a work of writing, art, or music
senses.example: Would you like a piece of cake?

senses.definition: to put separate parts together to make a whole
senses.example: We pieced together what happened.

senses.zh: 陆地；土地；国家（文学用法）
senses.definition: the solid surface of the earth, an area of ground, or a country in literary use
senses.example: The family owns a small piece of land.

senses.definition: to come down onto the ground or water, or succeed in getting something
senses.example: The plane landed safely.

senses.definition: happening or beginning a short time ago
senses.example: Have you seen any recent news about it?

senses.definition: to say or write what someone or something is like
senses.example: Can you describe the person you saw?

senses.definition: something made or sold, something caused by a process, or the result of multiplying numbers
senses.example: This shop sells local products.

senses.definition: a person trained to treat illness, or someone with a high academic degree
senses.example: The doctor told him to rest.

senses.zh: 篡改；修改（尤指为掩盖真相）
senses.definition: to change a document or image dishonestly, or alter something for a particular effect
senses.example: The photo had been doctored.
senses.note: 动词 doctor 常含不诚实地修改的意思；不要把它当成“治疗”。

senses.definition: a solid upright structure that surrounds, divides, or protects a space
senses.example: There is a picture on the wall.

senses.definition: a person receiving medical care
senses.example: The nurse helped the patient sit up.

senses.definition: able to wait calmly or deal with difficulties without becoming angry
senses.example: Please be patient while I check the details.

senses.definition: a person who works, especially one who does a particular kind of job
senses.example: The workers repaired the road.

senses.definition: information about recent events, or something newly told to someone
senses.example: I have some good news for you.
senses.note: news 虽以 s 结尾，通常作不可数名词；说 a piece of news。

senses.definition: a way to check knowledge, quality, or condition
senses.example: We have an English test on Friday.

senses.definition: to check how well something works, what someone knows, or whether a claim is true
senses.example: The lab tested the water.

senses.definition: a story shown as moving pictures, usually with sound
senses.example: We watched a movie last night.

senses.zh: 确定的；确信的；某些的；特定的
senses.definition: sure about something, or used to refer to a particular but unnamed person or thing
senses.example: I'm certain that she called yesterday.

senses.definition: the direction opposite south, or the northern part of a place
senses.example: The wind came from the north.

senses.definition: in or towards the northern part of a place
senses.example: They live on the north side of town.

senses.definition: towards or in the northern direction
senses.example: We drove north for three hours.

senses.definition: belonging to one person, concerning private matters, or based on direct experience
senses.example: Please keep your personal details safe.

senses.definition: in a plain or easy way, only, or used to emphasize a statement
senses.example: Simply press this button to start.

senses.definition: coming after second in a series
senses.example: She finished third in the race.

senses.definition: one of three equal parts, or the person or thing in third place
senses.example: A third of the class was absent.

senses.definition: coming in position three
senses.example: This is my third attempt.

senses.definition: the use of knowledge, tools, and methods to solve practical problems
senses.example: New technology has changed how we work.

senses.zh: 接住；抓住；赶上；感染；听清
senses.definition: to take hold of something moving, reach a vehicle in time, get an illness, or hear something correctly
senses.example: Can you catch the ball?

senses.definition: a hidden problem in an offer or an act of catching
senses.example: It sounds good, but what's the catch?

senses.definition: one movement of the foot, one stage of a process, or a raised level on stairs
senses.example: The first step is to write a plan.

senses.definition: to move a foot in a direction or put it on something
senses.example: Please step inside.

senses.definition: a very young child or animal
senses.example: The baby is sleeping.

senses.definition: very small or very young
senses.example: The farm has baby goats.

senses.definition: an electronic machine that stores information and carries out instructions
senses.example: My computer is running slowly.

senses.definition: a group of people or things that share qualities
senses.example: What type of music do you like?

senses.definition: to write using a keyboard
senses.example: Please type your name here.

senses.definition: the act of looking, listening, or thinking carefully about something
senses.example: Please pay attention to the signs.

senses.zh: 画；拉；抽取；吸引；打成平局
senses.definition: to make a picture with lines, pull something, take something out, attract interest, or finish a game level
senses.example: She likes to draw animals.

senses.definition: a game with no winner, a random selection, or something that attracts people
senses.example: The match ended in a draw.

senses.definition: a story shown as moving pictures, a material used to record images, or a thin layer covering something
senses.example: We saw a film at the cinema.

senses.definition: to make a moving-image recording of something
senses.example: They filmed the event for the school website.

author: root

senses.zh: 共和主义者；共和制支持者
senses.definition: a person who supports a republic rather than rule by a monarch
senses.example: He described himself as a republican.
senses.note: 小写 republican 泛指共和制支持者；美国共和党党员通常写作大写 Republican。

senses.definition: relating to a republic or to the idea that a country should have an elected head of state
senses.example: They supported republican reforms.
senses.note: 指美国共和党时通常写作大写 Republican。

notes: 小写 republican 通常泛指共和制；美国共和党党员及相关形容词常用大写 Republican。

evidence.note: Dictionary distinguishes general republican and US party usage.

senses.definition: a group formed for a purpose, or the way work is arranged and controlled
senses.example: She works for a local organization.
senses.note: 美式拼写 organization；英式也常拼 organisation。

senses.definition: a tall plant with a trunk and branches, or a diagram with branching parts
senses.example: There is an old tree in the garden.

senses.definition: the place where something comes from, or a person or document that provides information
senses.example: We checked the source of the story.

senses.definition: to obtain materials or products from a particular place
senses.example: The company sources its coffee locally.

senses.definition: having the colour of blood or becoming that colour
senses.example: The sky turned red at sunset.

senses.definition: the colour of blood, or a substance of that colour
senses.example: Red is her favourite colour.

senses.definition: almost, but not completely
senses.example: We nearly missed the train.

senses.definition: to decide which person or thing you want from several possibilities
senses.example: You can choose a book to read.

senses.definition: a reason why something happens, or an aim that people work to support
senses.example: We need to find the cause of the problem.

senses.definition: to make something happen
senses.example: The heavy rain caused flooding.

senses.definition: the thin strands that grow on a person's or animal's head or body
senses.example: She has long black hair.

senses.definition: a period of one hundred years
senses.example: This bridge was built in the last century.

senses.definition: facts or signs that help show whether something is true
senses.example: There is no evidence to support the claim.

senses.definition: to show that something exists or is true
senses.example: The change is evidenced by recent data.
senses.note: 动词 evidence 多见于正式书面语，日常表达常用 show。

senses.definition: an opening in a wall with glass, a time available for an action, or an area on a computer screen
senses.example: Please open the window.

senses.definition: hard to do, understand, or deal with
senses.example: This word is difficult to pronounce.

senses.definition: to pay attention to sounds or to what someone says
senses.example: Please listen carefully to the instructions.

senses.definition: in a short time from now or from a particular time
senses.example: The train will leave soon.

senses.definition: the way of life and ideas of a group, or cells grown for study
senses.example: Food is an important part of culture.

senses.definition: to grow cells or microorganisms for scientific study
senses.example: The lab cultured the bacteria overnight.
senses.note: 动词义用于实验室；日常学习重点是名词“文化”。

senses.definition: the number 1,000,000,000
senses.example: The project cost two billion dollars.

senses.definition: a quantity of one thousand million
senses.example: A billion is a thousand million.

senses.definition: an opportunity, the possibility of something happening, or an unplanned event
senses.example: Give her a chance to explain.

senses.definition: to risk doing something, or happen unexpectedly
senses.example: We chanced upon a quiet café.
senses.note: 动词义较少见，优先掌握名词“机会、可能性”。

senses.definition: a boy or man who has the same parents as another person
senses.example: My brother is older than I am.

senses.definition: the strength to do things, physical power, or a resource used to make heat and electricity
senses.example: The children still had energy to play.

senses.zh: 意识到；认识到；实现；变现
senses.definition: to understand a fact, make something hoped for happen, or turn an asset into money
senses.example: I realized that I had left my keys at home.
senses.note: 英式也常拼 realise；“意识到”是日常高频义。

senses.zh: 时期；一段时间；课时；句号（美）
senses.definition: a length of time, one lesson in a timetable, or the dot at the end of a sentence in US English
senses.example: The first period begins at nine.

senses.definition: the warmest season of the year
senses.example: We visit our grandparents every summer.

senses.definition: the number 100
senses.example: The school has two hundred students.

senses.definition: a group or amount of one hundred
senses.example: A hundred is enough for this exercise.

senses.zh: 可获得的；可使用的；有空的
senses.definition: able to be used, obtained, or met at a particular time
senses.example: Are you available for a call this afternoon?

senses.definition: a living thing that grows in soil, a factory, or equipment used in industry
senses.example: The plant needs more sunlight.

senses.definition: to put a seed or young plant in the ground, or place something somewhere
senses.example: We planted a tree in the garden.

senses.definition: expected to happen or probably true
senses.example: Rain is likely this evening.

senses.definition: probably
senses.example: She will likely arrive by six.
senses.note: 副词 likely 在美式英语更常见；英式也用 most likely 等形式。

senses.definition: a situation that makes it possible to do something useful or wanted
senses.example: This course is a good opportunity to practise speaking.

senses.zh: 术语；学期；期限；条件（复数）
senses.definition: a word used for an idea, a school period, a set length of time, or the conditions of an agreement
senses.example: We learned a new scientific term today.

senses.definition: to give someone or something a particular name, often a formal one
senses.example: The plan was termed a success.

senses.zh: 短的；矮的；不足的；简短的
senses.definition: not long in distance, time, or height, or less than needed
senses.example: We took a short walk after dinner.

senses.definition: less than a stated amount or before reaching a goal
senses.example: We stopped short of the bridge.

senses.zh: 短片；短裤（复数）；空头仓位
senses.definition: a short film or other short work, or a financial position that benefits when prices fall
senses.example: We watched a short before the main film.
senses.note: shorts（复数）表示短裤；金融里的 short 是专业义。

senses.definition: a written message sent to someone, or a symbol in an alphabet
senses.example: She wrote a letter to her friend.

senses.definition: the state something is in, a requirement for an agreement, or an illness
senses.example: The car is in good condition.

senses.definition: to train or prepare someone for a situation, or make hair soft with a product
senses.example: The athletes were conditioned for hot weather.

senses.definition: the act of deciding between things, the thing chosen, or the right to decide
senses.example: You have a choice between tea and coffee.

senses.definition: of especially good quality
senses.example: They served choice cuts of meat.
senses.note: 形容词 choice 用法较少，常见于 choice cuts 等固定搭配。

senses.definition: only one, not married or in a relationship, or not combined with others
senses.example: She bought a single ticket.

senses.definition: a song released on its own, a one-way ticket, or a person without a partner
senses.example: The band's new single is popular.

senses.zh: 挑出（通常与 out 连用）
senses.definition: to choose one person or thing from a group for special attention
senses.example: The teacher singled out her answer for praise.

senses.definition: an instruction about what is allowed, a usual pattern, or control by a leader
senses.example: The school has a rule about phones.

senses.definition: to govern a place, officially decide something, or control an activity
senses.example: The court ruled in her favour.

senses.definition: a female child of a parent
senses.example: Their daughter started school this year.

senses.definition: the work of organizing a business or service, or the government in office
senses.example: She works in school administration.

senses.definition: the direction opposite north, or the southern part of a place
senses.example: The south of the country is warmer.

senses.definition: located in or towards the southern part of a place
senses.example: They live on the south side of town.

senses.definition: towards or in the southern direction
senses.example: We drove south along the coast.

senses.definition: the man someone is married to
senses.example: Her husband cooked dinner tonight.

senses.zh: 节约使用；精心管理（正式）
senses.definition: to use a limited supply carefully so that it lasts
senses.example: They husbanded their resources during the long journey.
senses.note: 动词 husband 是正式用法；日常“节约”多用 save 或 conserve。

evidence.note: Cambridge lists formal verb meaning conserve resources.

senses.definition: a large formal meeting of representatives, or a national law-making body
senses.example: Delegates met at the congress to discuss the policy.
senses.note: 专指美国国会时一般写作 Congress，首字母大写。

senses.definition: the flat surface under your feet, a level of a building, or the right to speak in a meeting
senses.example: Their office is on the third floor.

senses.zh: 使震惊；把…打倒；使不知所措
senses.definition: to knock someone to the ground or surprise them greatly
senses.example: The news floored everyone in the room.
senses.note: 动词义多用于被动或非正式表达。

senses.definition: a planned series of actions to achieve a political, social, or military aim
senses.example: The school started a campaign to reduce waste.

senses.definition: to organize actions in public to achieve a change or win an election
senses.example: They campaigned for safer roads.

senses.definition: a substance used to make something, or information used for a particular purpose
senses.example: This bag is made from recycled material.

senses.definition: connected with physical things rather than ideas, or important to a decision
senses.example: The report found no material difference.

senses.definition: all the people living in a place, or all the members of an animal or plant group
senses.example: The city's population is growing.

senses.zh: 经济；经济体；节约；经济舱
senses.definition: the system of making and using money and goods, careful use of resources, or a lower-priced travel class
senses.example: The local economy depends on tourism.

senses.definition: connected with the study or treatment of illness
senses.example: She needs medical advice from a doctor.

senses.definition: a check of someone's health by a doctor, often before a job
senses.example: He had to pass a medical for the new job.
senses.note: 名词 medical 在英式英语较常见；美式常说 physical 或 medical examination。

evidence.note: Cambridge lists adjective and mainly UK noun for physical examination.

senses.definition: a place where people receive medical treatment, often staying overnight
senses.example: She works at the local hospital.
senses.note: 英式常说 in hospital；美式常说 in the hospital。

senses.definition: a building for Christian worship, the Christian community, or a religious service
senses.example: They visited the old church in the town centre.

senses.definition: to shut something, stop operating, finish an activity, or complete a business deal
senses.example: Please close the door when you leave.

senses.definition: near in distance or time, having a strong relationship, or almost equal
senses.example: She is a close friend of mine.

senses.definition: near someone or something
senses.example: Come close so you can hear me.

senses.definition: the end of something
senses.example: The meeting came to a close.

evidence.note: Cambridge distinguishes verb and noun from adjective and adverb senses.
Pronunciation differs: /z/ for verb/noun end, /s/ for adjective/adverb near.

senses.definition: the possibility of something bad happening, or an activity involving that possibility
senses.example: There is a risk of heavy rain.

senses.definition: to put something valuable in danger of being lost, or do something despite danger
senses.example: Do not risk your health for the job.

senses.definition: the number 1,000
senses.example: More than a thousand people attended.

senses.definition: a quantity of one thousand
senses.example: There were thousands at the event.

senses.definition: happening, existing, or used now
senses.example: What is your current address?

senses.definition: a moving flow of water or air, or electricity moving through a wire
senses.example: The river current was strong.

evidence.note: Cambridge lists adjective for present and noun for flowing water, air, electricity.

senses.definition: flames and heat from burning, an uncontrolled blaze, or shooting from weapons
senses.example: The fire spread quickly through the building.

senses.definition: to shoot a weapon, dismiss someone from a job, or make something burn
senses.example: The company fired him last month.

senses.definition: the time after the present, or what may happen then
senses.example: We are planning for the future.

senses.definition: belonging to or expected at a later time
senses.example: Future students may use this library.

senses.zh: 错误的；不合适的；不道德的
senses.definition: not correct, not suitable, or morally bad
senses.example: The answer is wrong.

senses.definition: in an incorrect way
senses.example: I wrote the date wrong.

senses.definition: an act that is morally bad or unfair
senses.example: We should try to right the wrong.

senses.definition: to treat someone unfairly
senses.example: She felt she had been wronged.
senses.note: 动词 wrong 多用于正式表达或被动结构。

evidence.note: Cambridge lists adjective, adverb, noun, and verb.
